findings.reason: §5's edit field list must add the route (and re-run the picker's override checks on it) or §15 must name the verb that does the re-route; as written the §5 implementer builds an edit that cannot re-route and §15's re-route mechanism is unreachable.
findings.text: §15 states "Re-routing a queued request is explicit, through `crew queue edit` (§5), never a background re-pick", but §5's specification of the verb (snapshot line 64) says `edit` "replaces an `awaiting-upstream` or queued request's steering text, done-when, write paths or time budget, re-runs the contract checks, and is refused once the request has launched" — the lane, backend and model are not among the fields, and §5's done-when tests only steering-text editing, so the one path §15 names for changing a queued request's route has no verb behind it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_priority_key` (`reckon/roadmap_ranking.py:196`, vocabulary order critical path, sprint position, ROI, reach, stuck as §4 states), `STARVATION_AGE_SECONDS` (`reckon/crew/queue_order.py:13`), `_dispatch_lane_allowance` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1565`, and its `lane_document`-or-`None` line as §15 relies on), `admit_once` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1049`), `crew view drain` (`drain` is a live view name), `imas-ambix:local-lane-admission-control#s27` (exists and declares the wait on this plan's §4), and §13's "user-global agent guidelines carry a dispatch paragraph" (`~/.agents/AGENTS.md` → `dotfiles/agents/AGENTS.md:687` "Dispatch through the Jev router") all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each changed node's done-when is measurable and carries a control: §4's equal-weights arm, §13's grep over `skills/` and `AGENTS.md`, §15's "routes no request to codex" arm, §9's "stores nothing"/"stores no pointer" assertions and §14's zero-violation counts.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §14's drain evidence lands on `docs/evidence/archive/a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan-landed.html`, which exists as the repository's per-plan archive convention; no changed unit names a scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, filename or comment, and no changed unit carries changelog prose; the state names (`awaiting-upstream`, `blocked-upstream`, `held`) name phases rather than a plan item.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §15 makes re-routing a queued request the job of `crew queue edit`, but §5, which defines that verb, does not list the route among the fields `edit` replaces.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §9 (load the width in one beat), §13 (the skills teach it), §14 (dogfood the drain), §15 (one queue with per-lane admission) each carry one deliverable; §15's routing and its per-lane admission are two faces of the same change to one queue.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every `plan-section-depends-on` edge resolves to a section that exists, the followup's build order matches the declared edges step for step, and §15's use of `crew queue edit` (§5) is reachable through s15→s4→s5; s14's closure reaches every other section.
